title: Your First 30 Days in an AJCC
description: A self-paced onboarding sequence a board can assign on day one: how the workforce system is organized, who the partners are, where local policies live, what security and confidentiality training is required (WSD24-12), how to shadow effectively, and when to escalate. Modeled on Virginia's three-week case-manager learning path.
notes: Audience: New hires, staff of newly awarded providers. Format: SP series (6 modules). Hours assumed from format (6 self-paced modules at about 1 hour each). Gap addressed: No standard California onboarding path; staff learn from whoever sits next to them.
learning_objectives: Describe the roles of the Local Board, AJCC Operator, Career Services Provider, EDD, and partners.
Locate their board's local policies and the state directives behind them.
Complete the CalJOBS access requirements and explain why they matter.
Follow a structured shadowing checklist and know which decisions require a supervisor.

sequencing_rationale: Lessons follow the catalog's learning objectives in the order a practitioner meets them on the job: How the Workforce System Is Organized; Who's Who: Board, Operator, Provider, EDD, and Partners; Finding Your Local Policies and the Directives Behind Them; CalJOBS Access, Security, and Confidentiality; Shadowing with Purpose; When to Escalate: Decisions That Need a Supervisor. There is no separate project lesson; each lesson ends in a practice exercise built on the same running case. Scope assumptions: hours are not stated in the source catalog and are assumed from the delivery format (SP series (6 modules); 6 self-paced modules at about 1 hour each). Content is grounded in California and federal guidance named in the catalog description and objectives; the course cites those directives by number but does not reproduce their text, and every policy-specific claim must be checked against the current directive before delivery. Local board policy is treated as a variable the learner fills in from their own board, not something the course prescribes. Design driver (catalog "gap addressed"): No standard California onboarding path; staff learn from whoever sits next to them. Statistics and audit findings quoted from the catalog have not been independently verified.
